cases.candidate_question: Assigning any value v at zero always produces a continuous extension.
cases.why_invalid: For f(x)=x and u=1, every nonzero quotient is 1; assigning v≠1 makes the extension discontinuous.

cases.candidate_question: A differentiable product necessarily has differentiable factors.
cases.why_invalid: The parameterized family in the card has a differentiable squared product and two nondifferentiable absolute-value factors.

cases.candidate_question: The exponential quotient derivative has a plus sign between the two numerator terms.
cases.why_invalid: For f=0 and g(x)=x at a=1 the derivative is -1, whereas the proposed plus sign gives 1.

cases.candidate_question: Two primitives of the same function must themselves be equal.
cases.why_invalid: The functions f(x)=x and g(x)=x+c, with c≠0, have equal derivatives but unequal values.

cases.candidate_question: The same family has unique minimum d at a even when c≤0.
cases.why_invalid: When c=0 every x is a minimizer; when c<0 the values become arbitrarily negative as |x-a| grows.

cases.candidate_question: A zero derivative at a point guarantees a local minimum.
cases.why_invalid: Every member of -c(x-a)² with c>0 instead has nearby strictly smaller values, as the card constructs.

cases.candidate_question: Every stationary point is a global minimizer without convexity.
cases.why_invalid: For f(x)=-(x-a)² the derivative at a is zero but every x≠a has a smaller value.

cases.candidate_question: The equivalence holds also for c=0.
cases.why_invalid: With a=0,b=1 and f(x)=1/x, the left interval collapses to 0..0 using total division; the right-hand function is not integrable near zero.

cases.candidate_question: The same integral formula holds after omitting the k term.
cases.why_invalid: For f=0 and g(x)=x on [0,1], the omitted-term integrand is zero but the endpoint difference is 1.

cases.candidate_question: The formula is valid with the correction term -1/c² removed.
cases.why_invalid: Differentiating (x/c)exp(cx) produces (x+1/c)exp(cx), including a nonzero unwanted term for c≠0.

cases.candidate_question: For every integrable f, the derivative of its indefinite integral equals f(a) at every point a.
cases.why_invalid: The parameterized nonzero point spike is integrable but has zero integral on every interval, contradicting pointwise equality at its spike.

cases.candidate_question: The mean value theorem needs differentiability only inside the interval, with no endpoint continuity.
cases.why_invalid: The endpoint-spike family on every a<b has interior derivative zero and nonzero endpoint secant slope.

cases.candidate_question: The left endpoint a always supplies the same derivative as the midpoint in this formula.
cases.why_invalid: For c≠0 and a<b, the derivative difference between the midpoint and a is c(b-a)≠0.

cases.candidate_question: The endpoint increment identity follows even if continuity at b is omitted.
cases.why_invalid: An endpoint spike equal to 1 at b and zero elsewhere has c=0 throughout (a,b) but endpoint increment 1.

cases.candidate_question: Mere strict increase of h suffices for the same positive quadratic lower bound c.
cases.why_invalid: For f(x)=x⁴ at a=0 the derivative 4x³ is strictly increasing, but x⁴≥c x² fails at sufficiently small nonzero x for any c>0.
